# Encounters with Bayl?s Warband

*Pages PDF 17-18*

WARBAND OF BAYL OF MANY EYES 

## **Encounters with Bayl’s Warband**
The full strength of Bayl’s forces will be far too much for an inexperienced band of Characters to deal with. Equally, experienced Characters might find a pair of Chaos Knight outriders little more than a distraction. Below you will find three different circumstances in which a portion of Bayl’s warband might be encountered. You should choose the most appropriate one for your group, or feel free to tailor these encounters further if a greater, or lesser, challenge is called for. 

Of course, clever (or reckless) adventurers may well work out that the behaviour of the outriders amounts to a distraction and head off to discover the main force of Bayl’s warband. They will come across signs of the warband’s movements before they encounter them and might deduce this large group of Chaos warriors is not keen to engage in unnecessary combat. The outriders consist of: 

0 4 Chaos Knights of Nurgle. 

## **The Outriders Easy Encounter**
Bayl’s warband are making their way from the Troll Country to the Southlands, crossing Kislev and the eastern provinces of the Empire to do so. The Chaos Knights in Bayl’s warband rove ahead of the main force, and then circle back to either side, checking the rear, and then round to the front again, making sure that nothing can approach the main force without meeting them first. 

Should a group of these knights come across an opponent such as an adventuring party they will act in a rather unexpected manner. One of the knights will pull forth a horn and give a series of piping signal calls, before the group of knights veer to the left and crash through the undergrowth as fast as their steeds can carry them. Such behaviour may well surprise adventurers, Chaos Warriors are feared as cruel and powerful raiders, but these ones seem averse to combat. 

A Character who passes a **Very Hard (-30) Language (Battle)** Test can glean a little information from the horn blasts. They are dissimilar to signals used by the militaries of the Old World, but would be effective in raising an alarm and giving a sense of direction. Such a character can also be informed (if it is not readily obvious to them) that the knights are not likely to be alone, given that a signal apparently needed to be given. 

The Knights hope to draw the adventurers after them, lose them, and then circle back to the main force. If the adventurers’ pursuit proves determined, half of the knights will turn and charge while the others make their escape. 

## **Beaten and Bedraggled Medium Encounter**
Warriors of Nurgle are tough and fearsome, but they still need to eat, and Bayl lacks anything in the way of supply lines as he carries out his quest. The Warband of Bayl cannot despoil the countryside as they travel, for to do so would be to attract too much attention and leave a trail that would be easily followed. However, when the warband do come across an area of farmland they split into small groups dedicated to foraging for food. 

Bayl is willing for his warriors to be more confrontational when foraging for food than they are on the move. The warband need to eat, and witnesses to their passage need to be silenced, so when foraging the band are split into groups that are more than capable of taking on a farmstead and carrying back food. 

If the characters come across a farmstead that has been raided they may be able to glean some idea of what happened. Prepared foodstuffs will all be missing, as well as a portion of any crops ripe for harvest. 

However, money and valuables will be left were they lie. All the people who lived on the farm are dead, raiders are careful to scour the area and leave no witnesses, and will have left the bodies of their victims piled up in a barn. 

Bayl’s Warriors attack in overwhelming force and have little to fear from their victims. However, should one of them die during a raid the body will be buried, as the Tribe of Bayl believes it pleases Nurgle for their remains to become food for worms. 

The Characters may come across the foraging party during a raid, or on their way back from one. A typical foraging party might include: 

- Two Chaos Knights acting as forward scouts and messengers. 

- Ten Chaos Warriors of Nurgle. 

- Five Chosen Warriors of Nurgle. 

## **We Need to Talk Hard Encounter**
There are not many reasons why Bayl would want to tangle with a party of adventurers. His drive to reach the Southlands precludes him from becoming embroiled in intrigues or challenging the enemies of Chaos. 

However, as his quest persists he is growing increasingly aware that he has only sparse information to go on. He knows a name, ‘Skrolk’, who he believes is a member of a ratlike species he has heard a great deal of rumour about. 

In this regard he may have a deal in common with the adventurers, who may well have come across evidence of the Skaven, but have little idea of what they are. Any information about the Ratmen will be of interest to Bayl. Should he learn of people in his vicinity with knowledge of them, he may be willing to devote a significant portion of his strength into tracking them down and finding out what they know. 

Bayl will still not be so reckless as to tackle the Characters in a built-up area such as a town or city. But should the adventurers be known to discuss the Skaven and happen to be travelling through the wilderness or staying in an isolated village, the whispers that guide Bayl southwards may direct him to their door. In such a case the warband will deploy as follows: 

   - Advance party of 20 Chaos Warriors of Nurgle led by Dónalegur. They will attempt to find and abduct the Characters as quickly and quietly as possible. 

   - Reserve force of 20 Warriors of Chaos and 10 Chosen of Chaos waiting on the outskirts of the village, ready to reinforce the advance party should they get into trouble). 

   - 16 Chaos Knights, ready to give chase should the Characters try to escape on horseback. 

   - Remaining force of 20 Warriors of Chaos and 10 Chosen of Chaos waiting in the woods with Bayl. This force will not commit to the attack, but try to continue the quest as best they can if the attack goes badly. 

- Dónalegur.
